$comment: 1c Pin Board — full masonry card inventory, in board order. These become 1000x1500 Pinterest pins. 'category' matches the board filter chips (All / Mechanism / Ritual / Evidence / Experts). 'source-page' is the suggested canonical URL the pin links back to. 'type' and 'image' are extra context for pin production; copy is final, do not edit before compliance review.

cards.headline: The 12-minute window
cards.body: Why the protocol is calibrated to twelve minutes, and what happens in tissue when you stop at eleven.
Cost per session over one year of daily use. A single clinic microcurrent visit averages €180.

cards.headline: Microcurrent needs moisture
cards.body: Conductivity is chemistry. What a conductive gel actually does, and why water alone underperforms.

cards.headline: Dr. Amara Osei — Clinical dermatology, Berlin
cards.body: The honest claim for home microcurrent is frequency. Daily, correctly dosed stimulation is something no monthly clinic visit can replicate.

cards.headline: What happens at 630 nanometres
cards.body: Cosmetic LED explained at the level of the mitochondrion. The wavelength, the dose, the study.

cards.headline: One mechanism, every Sunday. Pin it for later.
cards.body: The Protocol, weekly. No launches. No offers. One piece of skin science you can verify.

cards.headline: Read a label like a chemist
cards.body: A working method for cross-referencing ingredient claims against the papers they cite.

cards.headline: 630nm
cards.body: The red wavelength window where dermal penetration and mitochondrial response overlap.

cards.headline: Dr. Elena Vasquez — Photobiomodulation researcher
cards.body: At 630 to 660 nanometres the literature is genuinely strong. The variable that decides outcomes is not the device. It is adherence.

cards.headline: Consistency beats intensity
cards.body: The clinic delivers peaks. The instrument delivers frequency. Which one your skin remembers.

cards.headline: Recovery is a skin strategy
cards.body: Sleep, circulation and cortisol set the ceiling on any protocol. The physiology, briefly.

cards.headline: 12 min
cards.body: The full four-modality sequence. Calibrated so it survives contact with a real morning.

cards.headline: Maren Holt — Medical aesthetician, 14 yrs clinical
cards.body: I stopped selling single treatments. Tissue responds to sequence, not to events. Twelve minutes a day outperforms an hour a month.

cards.headline: The clinic dropout's guide
cards.body: What professional microcurrent costs per session, what it delivers, and where home output now stands.
